newsitem.title: Indonesia: Donetsk beats top seed Moscow in World Cities Chess.
newsitem.headline: Donetsk beats top seed Moscow in World Cities Chess.

text.p: The top seeded Moscow team suffered a major set-back when they defeated by Ukrainian rivals Donetsk in the sixth round of the inaugural World Cities Championship in Jakarta on Friday.
With both sides fielding only Grandmasters, a close tussle was expected and the first three boards fought each other to a standstill and agreed draws.
The match was decided on the fourth and final board when Moscow's Oleg Korneev exceeded the time limit and forfeited his game to Donetsk's Georgy Timoshenko.
Upon seeing that his clock registered a time forfeit Korneev threw the piece he was about to move onto the board, muttered a few words to his opponent and stormed from the playing arena.
Donetsk are now hot favourites to take the World Cities title and the $US10,000 first prize, having already played and beaten their two main rivals, Moscow and Oslo.

The sixth round featured a large number of lop-sided results, with Oslo destroying the young Filipino team Mandaluyung 4-0 to take clear second position and Bandung impressively outpointing Jakarta A by the same margin to move into a tie for third place with Moscow.
It was a bad day for the two Singapore teams, Sentosa and Raffles City, as both were convincingly defeated by Indonesian opponents.
However Hong Kong, languishing in second-last place at the half-way point of the event, moved up considerably after a whitewash of the Seychelles team Victoria.
Sydney disappointed yet again, only managing to draw with lowly ranked Medan. The World Cities Championship concludes on July 14.
